news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire reports 67 vacant surplus former operational assets against a portfolio of 549
news_drafts.lead:
Aberdeenshire Council had 67 vacant surplus former operational assets at the first quarter of 2026/27, according to the Business Services performance report for the Business Services Committee. Its operational portfolio, the buildings and sites it still uses, stands at 549 at the second quarter.

The paper says the number of vacant assets is expected to fall in 2026/27 and 2027/28. A number of closures are planned for early 2027, linked to a new depot and office facility at One Harlaw Road, Inverurie. The performance target for capital receipts, the money from selling assets, is 100% of the amount budgeted.

The committee also has the Business Services budget risk register for 2026/27. It identifies a pressure on income from licensing fees and charges. In the register's words, "Pressure has been identified within Licensing fees and charges however this is currently being offset with underspends across the wider Business Services budget." The risk score for council tax and fees-and-charges collection remains at 16, unchanged, with a residual score of 12.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire's climate emissions cuts fall 69% as LED streetlighting plan loses funding
news_drafts.lead: Aberdeenshire's Environment and Infrastructure Services Committee has scaled back its planned carbon reductions for 2026/27 from 81 tonnes to 25 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, after capital funding for LED streetlighting was not allocated. In its Carbon Budget progress update, the council identified the streetlighting rollout as the main project now unable to proceed. The committee acknowledged that meeting its climate change targets requires "significant capital investment" for which long-term funding has not yet been secured. Budget pressures, the council stated, can only be managed if additional funding becomes available to support the capital spending needed for those targets.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire IJB returns to surplus but remains dependent on partner funding
news_drafts.lead: The Aberdeenshire Integration Joint Board has closed a year-end surplus and created a small general fund reserve for the first time in the accounts to 31 March 2026, marking a marked improvement on the previous year through recovery activity, partner support and strengthened financial controls. The committee noted this was the beginning of a longer-term improvement rather than a final position. Officers confirmed that reserves available in the current financial year remained limited and the IJB continued to rely on partner funding to deliver a balanced budget while savings plans were implemented. External audit has identified medium-term financial sustainability as a key focus, reflecting structural challenges including demand pressures, workforce capacity constraints and the need for service redesign. The chief internal auditor provided the most positive opinion available under internal audit standards, confirming the IJB maintained an adequate and effective framework for governance, risk management and control during the year.

findings.headline: The resource implication recorded for the visitor levy action is "staff time
findings.detail: The action plan sets out the proposal and consultation work, led by a named officer, with an expected outcome of a proposal and public consultation within the stated timeline. The only resource implication recorded is staff time, and the paper contains no costed figures for the work or for expected levy income.
findings.matters: A finance director assessing whether a levy is a viable income source would look for costed preparation and yield estimates, and this paper contains neither.

findings.headline: Aberdeenshire's visitor levy proposal is still being developed, with the action to produce a proposal and public consultation planned to finish on 10 May 2027.
findings.detail: The paper is an update to Council on the visitor levy, covering work done so far, changes in legislation and a proposed timetable. It states that a full proposal is still being developed and that a statutory 12-week public consultation will follow if the report is agreed. Any local exemptions are to be decided by Full Council once the proposal is fully developed.
findings.matters: A visitor levy would be a new local revenue stream, and a finance director at another council following peer levy schemes can compare this timetable against their own.
findings.figures: Planned Start Thursday November 26, 2026; Planned Finish Monday May 10, 2027; statutory consultation of 12 weeks
findings.quote: A full proposal for a visitor levy is still being developed.

findings.headline: HRA forecast balanced for the full year at Q2, with a £2.269m Asset Management and Repairs pressure offset elsewhere
findings.detail: The paper says Tenancy Services (£1.746m) and Central Management (£0.719m) favourable variances offset the pressures. It also records a £1.281m reduction in forecast Second Homes Council Tax income due to project slippage and void costs at Kirkton, Fraserburgh.
findings.matters: A balanced HRA that relies on favourable offsets to cover a repairs pressure, with income slippage underneath, is a position that a finance director at another landlord council would compare to their own.
findings.figures: Balanced full-year forecast; £2.269m Asset Management and Repairs pressure; £1.746m Tenancy Services favourable; £0.719m Central Management favourable; £1.281m Second Homes Council Tax reduction
findings.quote: The HRA forecasts a balanced full-year position at Q2.

findings.headline: Council tax premium on homes empty over 12 months and second homes approved, effective 1 September 2026, with £2.2m of additional income in the budget
findings.detail: The paper says the Business Services Committee approved a 200% premium (300% total charge) for homes empty over 12 months and second homes. Impact is expected in monitoring data from October, and Council Tax remains on budget pending collection evidence.
findings.matters: A new premium that funds a budgeted income increase depends on collection evidence that will not show until later monitoring, which other councils considering similar premiums would want to see.
findings.figures: £2.2m additional income; 200% premium; 300% total charge; effective 1 September 2026
findings.quote: The budget includes £2.2m additional income, with the impact expected in monitoring data from October.

findings.headline: Forecast reserves of £110.950m at 31 March 2027, including £15.362m working balances
findings.detail: The paper states working balances remain in line with the approved Reserves Strategy at £13m General Fund and £2m HRA. The Transformation Reserve includes a £28.186m Payback Reserve not available for distribution.
findings.matters: The split between working balances, earmarked reserves and non-distributable amounts determines how much of the reserve total a council can actually draw on against the recurring gap.
findings.figures: £110.950m forecast reserves at 31 March 2027; £15.362m working balances; £13m General Fund working balance; £2m HRA working balance; £28.186m Transformation Payback Reserve
findings.quote: Forecast balance at 31 March 2027 is £110.950m, including £15.362m working balances.
